phases.name: Protocol And Safety
phases.goal: Add explicit frame abort support and keep committed-frame semantics intact.

phases.name: Sender Retry And Skip Rebuild Logic
phases.goal: Support whole-frame rollback with bounded per-file retries and terminal skips.

phases.name: Remove Disk Staging From Hot Path
phases.goal: Replace temp-file snapshots with in-memory small-file prefetch and direct large-file streaming.

phases.name: Ordered Parallel Walk
phases.goal: Parallelize directory listing in a bounded way without reintroducing full prescan.

phases.name: Dynamic Frames
phases.goal: Replace strict fixed-size frame behavior with a soft frame policy and reduced per-file flush pressure.

phases.name: Bench And Observability
phases.goal: Measure the new pipeline with enough detail to validate the redesign.

phases.name: Deferred Receiver Issue Journal Upload
phases.goal: Optionally send detailed skip journal data to the receiver after the core throughput work is stable.

tasks.title: Add FrameAbort and AbortAck protocol messages
tasks.summary: Extend the wire protocol with explicit messages for discarding the current uncommitted frame without reconnect-based control flow.
details: Add FrameAbort and AbortAck message variants to the protocol model.
Define message encoding, decoding, validation, and state-transition rules.
Document when sender is allowed to issue FrameAbort and what receiver must guarantee before AbortAck.
deliverables: Protocol enums and codec updated for FrameAbort and AbortAck.
Protocol documentation updated with new message sequence and invariants.
Protocol tests covering roundtrip encode and decode.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol codec roundtrips FrameAbort and AbortAck.
Receiver rejects malformed or out-of-order abort messages.
Documentation matches the implemented message flow.

tasks.title: Implement receiver-side explicit frame rollback
tasks.summary: Teach the receiver to truncate the partial archive back to the last committed boundary when a frame is explicitly aborted.
details: Track the transient frame state needed to discard uncommitted bytes safely.
On FrameAbort, truncate archive back to the last committed archive_len.
Clear transient frame checksum and byte counters before replying AbortAck.
deliverables: Rollback tests for a partially written frame.
acceptance_criteria: After FrameAbort, the receiver archive length equals the last committed archive_len.
No uncommitted bytes remain on disk after AbortAck.
Normal committed-frame behavior remains unchanged.

tasks.title: Implement sender-side explicit frame abort flow
tasks.summary: Allow sender session logic to discard the current frame in-band and resume rebuilding without reconnecting.
details: Add a sender helper that emits FrameAbort and waits for AbortAck.
Replace reconnect-as-control-flow assumptions in the future rollback path.
Surface abort statistics for later bench reporting.
deliverables: Session tests that abort and rebuild a frame without reconnect.
acceptance_criteria: Sender can abort an uncommitted frame and continue the same session.
AbortAck mismatch or failure is surfaced as a hard error.
Existing finish and ack flows still pass.

tasks.title: Introduce frame rebuild state machine with file attempt tracking
tasks.summary: Refactor sender frame construction so a mid-file failure triggers frame rollback and rebuild while preserving per-file retry counters.
details: Track the current frame start boundary and the file currently being streamed.
Persist per-file attempt counters across frame rebuilds within the same dump session.
Restart frame construction from the last committed boundary after AbortAck.
deliverables: Regression tests for rebuild after a retryable file failure.
acceptance_criteria: A retryable file failure does not corrupt the committed archive.
Frame rebuild resumes from the last committed frame boundary, not from process start.
Attempts for the failing file increment across rebuilds.

tasks.title: Enforce terminal skip after three failed file attempts
tasks.summary: After three failed attempts, stop rebuilding the same file forever and mark it skipped for the current dump.
details: Keep the retry budget fixed at three attempts per file.
After the third failure, mark the file terminally skipped.
Ensure skipped files still allow deterministic progress across later reconnects and resumes.
deliverables: Terminal skip path integrated with frame rebuild logic.
Tests for repeated failure followed by skip.
acceptance_criteria: A file is not attempted more than three times per dump.
After terminal skip, the dump continues with later files.
Skipped files do not cause endless abort and rebuild loops.

tasks.title: Add sender-side issue journal model
tasks.summary: Record terminal skip details locally so the dump has structured diagnostics beyond aggregate counters.
details: Define a sender issue journal entry with file_index, path, attempts, reason, and last_error.
Append a journal entry whenever a file reaches terminal skip.
Expose the journal in sender-side reporting without blocking the core throughput changes.
deliverables: Sender report updated to expose journal data or a stable local artifact.
acceptance_criteria: Every terminal skip produces exactly one issue journal entry.
Aggregate skip counters stay consistent with detailed journal entries.
Sender output remains backward-compatible unless intentionally versioned.

tasks.title: Add in-memory prefetch path for small files
tasks.summary: Preserve file-level parallelism for tiny files without paying the temp-file staging cost.
details: Replace disk-backed staging for small files with bounded in-memory buffers.
Keep reader-pool parallelism for the small-file path.
Introduce a tunable threshold that decides whether a file uses the in-memory path.
deliverables: Tests for bounded memory behavior on small files.
acceptance_criteria: Small files no longer require temp files in the normal hot path.
Memory use is bounded by configured concurrency and threshold.
The small-file path preserves retry and skip semantics.

tasks.title: Add direct streaming path for large files
tasks.summary: Stream large files from the source handle directly into tar, zstd, and network so sender temp disk is no longer a limiting resource.
details: Read large files directly from the opened source handle in the sender hot path.
Keep size_at_open semantics for tar header sizing and retry logic.
On mid-file failure, trigger frame abort and rebuild.
deliverables: Regression tests for mid-file failure and rebuild.
acceptance_criteria: Large files can be sent without creating temp snapshots proportional to file size.
Mid-file failure on the large-file path correctly aborts and rebuilds the frame.
Large-file successful sends still produce a valid archive.

tasks.title: Remove temp-file snapshots from the default fast path
tasks.summary: Once the new small-file and large-file paths are stable, stop relying on staged temp files for normal production sends.
details: Remove or demote create_staged_file from the main runtime path.
Delete now-unused temp-file cleanup logic from the fast path.
Update runtime documentation to match the new data paths.
deliverables: Fast path no longer depends on temp-file staging.
Documentation updated to describe the new runtime behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The production send path does not create temp file snapshots in the common case.
Documentation no longer claims disk staging for the normal fast path.
Regression suite still passes for sender and receiver flows.

tasks.title: Implement bounded async directory listing pool
tasks.summary: Prepare directory entries in parallel while keeping a single coordinator responsible for deterministic DFS output order.
details: Add a bounded directory listing pool that prepares sorted entry lists for directories.
Ensure the traversal coordinator remains the only source of truth for DFS order and file_index assignment.
Avoid unbounded accumulation of directory listings in memory.
deliverables: Deterministic order tests comparing old and new traversal output.
acceptance_criteria: Traversal order remains identical to the current deterministic DFS order.
The number of in-flight directory tasks is bounded.
No full pending-file prescan is reintroduced.

tasks.title: Integrate ordered async walk with PendingFrameFiles
tasks.summary: Feed the prepared directory listings into the existing pending-file pipeline without materializing the full file set.
details: Refactor PendingFileWalker and PendingFrameFiles to consume asynchronously prepared directory listings.
Keep resume validation intact when the committed prefix is skipped.
Preserve deterministic boundaries used by frame rebuild and resume.
deliverables: Resume regression tests for the new traversal path.
acceptance_criteria: PendingFrameFiles still yields files in stable order.
Resume validation still detects source mismatch correctly.
The send path does not require a full prescan.

tasks.title: Add traversal wait metrics
tasks.summary: Instrument the new walk so benchmarks can tell whether directory preparation still stalls the send path.
details: Measure coordinator wait time for directory listings.
Measure queue depth or in-flight directory task count.
Expose these metrics to the benchmark layer.
acceptance_criteria: Bench runs can report traversal wait time.
Instrumentation overhead stays low enough for matrix usage.
Metrics distinguish listing wait from file read and compress time.

tasks.title: Introduce soft frame policy abstraction
tasks.summary: Replace the implicit fixed-size frame behavior with an explicit policy object that can consider bytes, file count, and file risk.
details: Define frame policy inputs: soft_target_bytes, max_files_per_frame, large_file_single_frame_threshold, retried_file_isolated.
Make the sender ask the policy whether to continue or close the current frame after a completed file.
Keep frame boundaries aligned to completed files.
acceptance_criteria: Frame closing is driven by a policy, not a single hard coded byte check.
The policy can isolate large and retried files.
Committed frame semantics remain unchanged.

tasks.title: Reduce mandatory per-file zstd flush pressure
tasks.summary: Stop flushing the encoder at every file boundary and only flush or finish when the frame policy requires it.
details: Remove the unconditional flush on every completed file from the hot path.
Keep correctness for frame end and ack boundaries.
Verify that compression batching improves without corrupting frame semantics.
deliverables: Tests for valid frame output without per-file flush.
acceptance_criteria: The hot path no longer flushes zstd for every file by default.
Frame output remains valid and resumable.
Bench results can observe reduced flush count.

tasks.title: Isolate large and previously retried files into dedicated frames
tasks.summary: Bound rollback blast radius by giving risky files their own frames when the policy decides it is practical.
details: Force single-file frames for files above the configured large-file threshold.
Allow the policy to isolate a file after it has already failed once.
Keep the policy compatible with the existing completed-file-only frame boundary rule.
deliverables: Dedicated-frame handling for large and retried files.
acceptance_criteria: Large files can be isolated into their own frames.
Previously retried files can be isolated when policy requires it.
Rollback after a risky file failure does not discard unrelated committed frames.

tasks.title: Extend bench raw and summary schema for redesign metrics
tasks.summary: Add enough telemetry to prove whether the redesign actually fixes the expected bottlenecks.
details: Add traversal wait time, frame abort count, frame rebuild count, skipped file count, per-frame file count, ack wait time, and flush count.
Propagate the new fields through raw CSV, summary CSV, and markdown tables.
Add schema tests for parse, aggregate, and output compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: New metrics are present in raw and summary outputs.
CSV parsing and aggregation tests cover the new fields.
Documentation reflects the current bench schema.

tasks.title: Rerun matrix and document post-redesign recommendations
tasks.summary: Once the new pipeline lands, rerun the matrix and replace assumptions with measured conclusions.
details: Rerun the coarse matrix across all agreed datasets.
Compare manySmallFiles scaling before and after the redesign.
Update BENCH.md, README.md, and PERFOMANCE_UPDATE.md with measured conclusions and any revised defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Post-redesign matrix results are recorded.
Documentation describes measured outcomes rather than planned behavior.
Recommended defaults are justified by current data.

tasks.title: Optionally upload detailed issue journal to receiver
tasks.summary: Add a later-phase protocol tail that transfers the detailed skip journal to the receiver after the core throughput work is stable.
details: Design a compact protocol message sequence for issue journal upload.
Persist the received issue journal next to the final archive.
Keep this work deferred until the throughput redesign and measurements are complete.
deliverables: Deferred protocol design for issue journal upload.
Receiver-side persistence of the uploaded journal.
acceptance_criteria: Detailed journal upload is optional and does not block the core send path.
Receiver can store the uploaded journal alongside the dump.
Protocol documentation clearly marks this as post-core work.
